summary: 古埃及浮雕留下远航蓬特的线索，红海岸边洞穴里的船材、船锚、绳索和铭文补上了实物证据。研究者据此重建可拆装船只的远航方式，并追问航行何以少见。
logic: 港口洞穴出土航海遗物
推测船只拆装与远航频率

paragraphs.brief: 刻在埃及一座寺庙的墙上的景象始于公元前十五世纪讲述了一场惊人的海上航行从一个神秘的土地上，被称为蓬特，或上帝之地。
sentences: The scenes carved into a wall of an Egyptian temple dating from the 15th century BC tell of a remarkable sea voyage from a mysterious land known as Punt, or Land of God.
刻在埃及一座寺庙的墙上的景象始于公元前十五世纪讲述了一场惊人的海上航行从一个神秘的土地上，被称为蓬特，或上帝之地。
They show a fleet of ships bearing exotic cargo, navigating through high-crested waves on a journey.
他们展示了一队载运异国货物的舰队在旅途中穿过高密度的波浪
The exact meaning of these detailed carvings has divided Egyptologists ever since they were discovered in the mid-19th century.
这些详细的雕刻的确切含义已经分裂了埃及科学家自从他们在19世纪中叶被发现以来
Some people have argued that Punt was not on the sea, or was a fictitious place altogether, says Oxford University Egyptologist John Baines.
牛津大学埃及学家约翰·贝恩斯(John Baines)说：“有些人认为Punt不在海上。”
However, a series of remarkable discoveries on a desolate stretch of Egypt’s Red Sea coast has settled the debate.
然而，关于埃及红海海岸一片荒凉地带的一系列引人注目的发现，解决了这场辩论。
“These finds remove all doubt that you reach Punt by sea,” Baines says.
Baines说，“这些都排除了人们对你从海上到达Punt的怀疑”。
“The Egyptians must have had considerable seagoing experience.”
“埃及人一定有丰富的航海经验。”

paragraphs.brief: 一位在公元前1800年左右统治埃及的法老阿门哈特三世(Amenehat III)的陶器碎片帮助团队确定了洞穴的年龄。
sentences: The archaeologists behind these discoveries are Kathryn Bard of Boston University, USA, and Rodolfo Fattovich of Orientale University, Italy.
这些发现背后的考古学家是美国波士顿大学的Kathryn Bard和意大利东方大学的Rodolfo Fattovich。
From 2002 they spent several weeks each year examining a dried-up lagoon known in Egypt as Mersa Gawasis, and the coastal cliffs nearby.
从2002年起，他们每年花几个星期时间检查埃及的一个干涸的环礁湖，即Mersa Gawasis，以及附近的沿海悬崖。
They were searching for signs of a harbour that might have sheltered merchant ships like those depicted in the wall carvings.
他们正在寻找一个港口的痕迹，这个港口可能庇护了像墙上的雕刻一样的商船。

Finally, in December 2004, Bard was clearing what she thought was the back wall of a rock shelter when she put her hand through the sand into an open space and uncovered a hemispherical cave about 5 metres across and 2 metres high.
最后，在2004年12月，巴德正在清理她以为是岩石掩体的后墙，当时她将手伸入一个开放的空间，并发现了一个大约5米宽和2米高的半球洞穴。
The cave’s entrance was carved into an exact rectangle and was clearly not a natural formation.
洞穴的入口被刻成一个完全的矩形，显然不是自然形成的。
Inside, the archaeologists found shattered storage jars, broken boxes made from cedar planks, and five grinding stones.
考古学家在里面发现了破碎的储存罐子碎碎的箱子由雪松木板制成和五颗磨碎的石头
A pottery fragment inscribed with the name of Amenemhat III, a pharaoh who ruled Egypt around 1800 BC, helped the team pinpoint the cave’s age.
一位在公元前1800年左右统治埃及的法老阿门哈特三世(Amenehat III)的陶器碎片帮助团队确定了洞穴的年龄。

paragraphs.brief: 一个洞穴里有数百米的绳子精巧地缠绕着堆叠着
sentences: Not long afterwards, Bard and Fattovich came across a larger cave, reinforced with old wooden timbers and stone anchors—the first conclusive evidence of large-scale Egyptian seafaring ever discovered.
不久之后，巴德和法特维奇发现了一个更大的洞穴，用旧木木和石锚加固——这是埃及大规模航海史上首次发现的确凿证据。
Over the next few years, they uncovered the hidden remnants of an ancient boat-building and seafaring community.
在未来几年里，他们发现了一个古老的造船和航海社区的隐蔽残余物。
Many of the artefacts found were full of holes—the work of tiny marine animals known as shipworms.
发现的许多手工艺品都是洞—— 被称作船虫的小型海洋动物的工作。
In addition to eight caves, Bard and Fattovich found remains of five mud-brick ramps that might have been used to ease ships into the water.
除了8个洞穴之外，巴德和法特维奇还发现了5个泥砖坡道的残骸，这些坡道可能被用来使船只容易进入水中。
One cave contained hundreds of metres of rope, expertly coiled and stacked.
一个洞穴里有数百米的绳子精巧地缠绕着堆叠着

paragraphs.brief: 将Mersa Gawasis 和Punt 连接在一起的材料聚集在洞穴内外
sentences: Material connecting Mersa Gawasis to Punt accumulated both inside and outside the caves.
将Mersa Gawasis 和Punt 连接在一起的材料聚集在洞穴内外
A few hundred metres from the cliffs lie piles of crumbled stone and conch shells—most probably the remains of altars.
离悬崖几百米远的地方是一堆碎石和海螺壳——很可能是祭坛的残骸。
Among these are stones carved with inscriptions that specifically mention missions to Punt.
其中包括刻有具体提到对蓬特的访问的刻文的石头。
As if that weren’t enough, among the remnants found outside one cave were two planks marked with directions for assembling a ship.
似乎这还不够在一个洞穴外发现的残骸中有两块木板标着船的装配方向
One of them bore an inscription still partly legible after 3,800 years: “Year 8 under his majesty the king of Upper and Lower Egypt…given life forever…of wonderful things of Punt.”
其中一人在3800年之后仍然有一段可读的文字："在上埃及和下埃及国王陛下的统治下，第八年... 永远地... 赋予普特的美好生活...

paragraphs.brief: 虽然Mersa Gawasis 手工艺品回答了一些问题，但他们提出了其他问题。
sentences: While the Mersa Gawasis artefacts have answered some questions, they have raised others.
虽然Mersa Gawasis 手工艺品回答了一些问题，但他们提出了其他问题。
For instance, how did the expeditions to Punt actually work, and how did the Egyptians construct vessels that could make a round-trip voyage of over 3,000 kilometres?
例如，去往蓬特的远征究竟如何组织？埃及人又是怎样造出能够往返航行逾 3,000 公里的船只的？
Cheryl Ward, a maritime archaeologist at Coastal Carolina University in South Carolina, USA, has gone some way towards answering these questions.
美国南卡罗来纳州沿海卡罗莱纳大学的海洋考古学家谢丽尔·沃德，已经在某种程度上回答了这些问题。
She spent three years building a full-scale reconstruction of a ship that would have docked in the lagoon of Mersa Gawasis.
她花了三年时间建造了一艘可以停靠在梅萨加瓦西湖的全面重建的船
Ward has determined that, unlike modern vessels, the Egyptian ship was essentially one giant hull.
沃德已经确定，与现代船只不同，埃及的船基本上是一个巨大的船体。
The Egyptian ships were also unique in that they were held together with fittings that needed no metal fasteners, and could be taken apart and put back together again.
埃及船只也是独一无二的，因为它们与不需要金属紧固装置的配件一起被扣押，可以拆卸并重新组合在一起。
“From the very beginning, the Egyptians were building boats that could be disassembled, and that makes them different from anyone else,” Ward says.
沃德说，“从一开始，埃及人就正在造船，可以拆卸，这使他们与其他人不同。”

paragraphs.brief: 最后一个使用环礁湖的水手把他们的装备和掩体封在泥砖和沙子后面等待从未到来的探险
sentences: For all the skill and craftsmanship evident in the Mersa Gawasis caves, ancient Egypt’s ocean voyages were most likely an exception to the usual modes of trade, born out of a necessity to obtain precious materials such as incense and aromatic resins.
古埃及的海洋航行很可能是正常贸易方式的例外，而通常贸易方式的诞生是为了获得香和香树脂等珍贵材料。
For most of Egypt’s history these goods had moved along established routes across the eastern desert and through modern-day Sudan.
埃及的大部分历史都记载这些货物沿穿越东部沙漠的固定路线和经过现代苏丹。
But around the time Mersa Gawasis came into use, it seems a hostile new kingdom to the south cut Egypt off from its supply of exotic materials.
南方似乎是一个敌对的新王国，切断埃及的外来材料供应。

“If they could have gone overland, it would have been much easier than bringing timbers from Lebanon, building ships on the upper Nile, taking them apart and carrying them across the desert,” Bard says.
巴德说：“在尼罗河上游造船，拆卸船体，在沙漠中携带船体：“如果它们经过陆地，就比从黎巴嫩运来木材容易得多。”
“They weren’t stupid—no one wants to do things the hard way.
他们不傻，没人想做艰难的事情。
But geopolitically, they had no other choice.”
但从地缘政治上讲，他们别无选择。”
Fattovich suggests that there were probably only 15 to 20 expeditions over some 400 years—about one every two decades.
Fattovich表示，在大约400年的时间里，大概只有15至20次探险，大约每20年一次。
After that Mersa Gawasis fell out of use, probably because either there was no longer enough water in the lagoon to float ships, overland links improved, or alternative sites were found.
在那之后，Mersa Gawasis 失去了使用，可能是因为要么环礁湖的水已经不够漂浮，陆地连接得到改善，或者找到了替代地点。
The last sailors to use the lagoon sealed up their equipment and shelters behind mud bricks and sand to await expeditions that never came.
最后一个使用环礁湖的水手把他们的装备和掩体封在泥砖和沙子后面等待从未到来的探险

items.en: possible reasons why the site of Mersa Gawasis was abandoned
items.zh: Mersa Gawasis场址被废弃的可能原因
items.why: F段列出港口废弃的几种可能：潟湖水深不足、陆路改善，或找到了其他地点。

items.en: mention of a lack of agreement about an archaeological discovery
items.zh: 提及对考古发现缺乏一致意见
items.why: 自浮雕被发现起，埃及学家就为其确切含义意见分歧，符合“对考古发现看法不一”。

items.en: reference to a study which involved copying ancient Egyptian boat-building techniques
items.zh: 提及一项涉及复制古埃及造船技术的研究
items.why: 研究者花三年按实物大小重建一艘古船，以复制当时的造船方法检验其可行性。

items.en: a reason why the ancient Egyptians needed to import goods by sea
items.zh: 一个古埃及人需要从海上进口货物的原因
items.why: 南方敌对王国可能截断了原有陆路货源，埃及人为了取得香料等珍贵物资只得改走海路。

items.en: Illustrations of merchant ships sailing from Punt were found on wall carvings in an ancient ________ in Egypt.
items.zh: 在埃及一座古代________的墙面浮雕中，发现了从蓬特驶来的商船图像。
items.why: 回到对应内容“刻在埃及一座寺庙的墙上的景象始于公元前十五世纪讲述了一场惊人的海上航行从一个神秘的土地上，被称为蓬特，或上帝之地”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Bard and Fattovich hoped to find evidence of a ________ in the area of Mersa Gawasis.
items.zh: 巴德和法托维奇希望在梅尔萨加瓦西斯一带找到曾有________的证据。
items.why: 回到对应内容“他们正在寻找一个港口的痕迹，这个港口可能庇护了像墙上的雕刻一样的商船”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: When Bard first discovered a cave at Mersa Gawasis, the shape of its ________ indicated that it was man-made.
items.zh: 巴德最初在梅尔萨加瓦西斯发现一处洞穴时，根据其________的形状判断它是人工开凿的。
items.why: 回到对应内容“洞穴的入口被刻成一个完全的矩形，显然不是自然形成的”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Bard and Fattovich discovered a considerable number of objects that had been made by small sea creatures known as ________.
items.zh: 巴德和法托维奇发现了大量由一种叫作________的小型海洋生物造成的物件。
items.why: 回到对应内容“发现的许多手工艺品都是洞—— 被称作船虫的小型海洋动物的工作”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Ancient Egyptian sea voyages were probably relatively infrequent.
items.zh: 古埃及的海上航行可能相对较少。

items.en: It is now certain that the ancient Egyptians sailed to Punt.
items.zh: 现在可以肯定古埃及人已经开往蓬特了

items.en: During a certain period, Egyptians were forced to use sea rather than overland trade routes.
items.zh: 在一段时期里，埃及人被迫使用海运而不是陆路贸易路线。

items.en: It has been suggested that Punt never existed.
The construction of ancient Egyptian ships was unlike any other.
items.zh: 古埃及船只的建造与其他船只不同。

points: F段列出港口废弃的几种可能：潟湖水深不足、陆路改善，或找到了其他地点。
回到对应内容“他们正在寻找一个港口的痕迹，这个港口可能庇护了像墙上的雕刻一样的商船”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: …, says Oxford University Egyptologist John Baines.
“Some people have argued that Punt was not on the sea, or was a fictitious place altogether”补足 says 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 says 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
连接词 while 引出“While the Mersa Gawasis artefacts have answered some questions”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Archaeological discoveries on Egypt’s Red Sea coast indicate that the region’s ancient inhabitants were a skilled seafaring people.
埃及红海沿岸的考古发现表明，该地区的古老居民是熟练的航海者。
